en.title: Path Visiting Vertices in Numeric Order
en.description:
Determine whether the graph contains a path 1—2—…—N made of direct edges. All vertices must be visited in ascending order, and a detour through other vertices cannot replace the direct edge between consecutive numbers.

The input protocol, the ranges added by this site, the examples, and the tests were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input: the first line contains N M (1≤N≤100000, 0≤M≤200000), followed by M lines, each describing a simple undirected edge u v, with vertices numbered 1..N.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: 1—2, 2—3, and 3—4 all exist, so output 1.

Example 2: the direct edge 1—2 is missing, so even though the graph is connected the required walk is impossible; output 0.

Example 3: a single vertex already forms the path and needs no edges; output 1.
hints: Collect the edges whose endpoints differ by 1 and check whether they cover all N−1 pairs of consecutive numbers.
